subject: Hosted vs incumbent: p95/p99 end-to-end latency qualification playbook
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Nina Rao <nina@novamed.ai>, Ops Team <ops@novamed.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Subject: Hosted vs incumbent: p95/p99 end-to-end latency qualification playbook

Hi Nina / NovaMed Ops — thanks for the time today. Quick recap of the call and agreed next steps so we have a single playbook for qualification: 

1) High-level targets (we discussed both single-turn and streaming flows):
   - Single-turn generation (short prompts, <= 128 tokens): target hosted p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 280 ms (end-to-end, client -> Redwood hosted API -> model -> response)
   - Multi-turn streaming conversation (average turn ~64 tokens, KV cache warm): target hosted p95 <= 160 ms, p99 <= 420 ms for first-byte streaming; per-token steady-state streaming tail expectations to be measured separately.
   - Peak concurrency target: 1,200 concurrent requests across your API gateway (burst to 2,000 for 60s tolerated)
   - Throughput envelope: steady-state 300 reqs/s, peak 600 reqs/s (see attached traffic envelope CSV for minute-by-minute profile)

2) What we heard about your incumbent baseline:
   - VendorX current baselines reported by your SRE: p95 ~210 ms, p99 ~520 ms on single-turn; streaming first-byte p95 ~290 ms.
   - Amplifying factors: request fanout for multi-step reranking and synchronous embedding calls.

3) Redwood qualification plan (summary):
   - We will replicate your traffic envelope (attached) against both endpoints (your current vendor endpoint and Redwood hosted API) using the same client harness and tokenization.
   - Run types: cold-start (KV empty), warmed-KV steady-state, and burst-surge test. For streaming, emulate real client-side connection patterns (60–120 ms client read windows).
   - Metrics we will capture: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, first-byte latency for streaming, per-token throughput, error rates, and tail correlation with sequence length.

4) Immediate asks from NovaMed to get started:
   - Share canonical traffic envelope CSV (minute granularity) and a sample of representative prompts (PII redacted).
   - Provision a short-lived API key for Redwood test harness to hit VendorX and Redwood-hosted (we will not persist customer data).
   - Confirm a 2-hour engineering sync early next week to align test runners and any gateway headers.

Attachments: p95p99-traffic-envelope.csv (attached)

Next steps (for Redwood): Ben will draft the test-run runbook and resource requirements; Laura will coordinate scheduling and procurement touches; Jasmine will own demo/engineering sync invites.

Thanks — Ill follow up with a calendar invite.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks Nina — good context. Quick technical runbook outline well use for the comparison tests (attaching fuller PDF runbook):

1) Harness and tokenization
   - We will run a single harness that first tokenizes using the canonical tokenizer you provide, then replays requests at the same token counts against both endpoints. This removes tokenization variance.

2) Test scenarios (each run = 30 minutes, repeated 3x across different cluster hours)
   - Cold-start (cluster idle): 5 req/s ramp to 300 req/s over 3m, hold 10m, collect tails.
   - Warm-KV steady-state: pre-warm KV caches with 1m warm-up, then 300 req/s steady for 20m.
   - Burst-surge: steady 300 req/s with 60s 2k req/s spike.
   - Streaming emulation: open 1.2k concurrent SSE/websocket clients; average turn 64 tokens; send partials to exercise first-byte behavior and per-token tail.

3) Data collection and comparisons
   - Collect p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end, first-byte latency for streaming, per-token throughput, error rates, and 95/99 percentiles of connection setup latency.
   - Cross-compare bucketed by sequence length (<=64, 65-256, >256) and by request type (single-turn, multi-step rerank, embed).

4) Success criteria (suggested)
   - Hosted p95 <= VendorX p95 * 0.9 AND hosted p99 <= VendorX p99 (strict tail parity). Alternatively, documented regression windows with rollback plan if minor regression only at very long sequences.

5) Logistics and keys
   - Please provide a scoped test key for VendorX endpoint and a scoped key we can use against your gateway to mirror their traffic. We will delete keys after tests.
   - We will publish a shared results dashboard (temporary) and an executive summary.

Attachment: runbook-latency-playbook.pdf (PDF, 124 KB)

Ill kick off the harness preparation today and aim to run the first baseline later this week UTC hours. Propose engineering sync: Tue 2028-03-21 15:00 PT — does that work for your SRE?

—Ben
